newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-AUSTRALIAN CLUBS WIDEN LEAGUE SPLIT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-AUSTRALIAN CLUBS WIDEN LEAGUE SPLIT.

text.p: The bitter split within Australian rugby league hardened on Wednesday when 12 top clubs vowed to prolong their fight against Rupert Murdoch's breakaway Super League for another season.
National champions Manly led a formal commitment by the clubs to play in the long-established Australian Rugby League (ARL) premiership in 1998.
The agreement, announced at a news conference at ARL headquarters, ended speculation that several clubs might switch to Super League next season.
It also strengthens the ARL's bargaining position in any future negotiations aimed at unifying the sport in Australia, the world's strongest playing nation.
Media magnate Murdoch launched Super League in Australia in March in direct competition with the ARL after a bitter two-year power struggle.
But attendances and television ratings have fallen sharply in a backlash by fans disgruntled by months of feuding between players and administrators.
